name: Cottage cheese protein brownies (fudgy, flourless)

source.author: Hebrew recipe (screenshot) — ingredients listed, NO quantities given
source.notes: The caption named the 5 ingredients (cottage, egg white, peanut butter, honey, cocoa) but gave no amounts. Quantities here are reference-grounded (typical flourless cottage-cheese protein brownie ratios) then TUNED for ideal macros: cottage maxed for protein, lean egg WHITES (per the caption) instead of whole eggs, peanut butter moderated to 2 tbsp (calorie-dense), honey moderated to 3 tbsp (main sugar source), cocoa ⅓ cup for chocolate flavor + micros (iron/magnesium/polyphenols). Cottage assumed 5% fat. Yields ~9 brownies in an 8×8 pan.

ingredients.note: lean protein + binding (caption's choice vs whole egg)
moderated — main sugar; cut to 2 tbsp or part-stevia for less

steps: Blend cottage cheese, egg whites, peanut butter and honey smooth; blend in cocoa, vanilla, baking powder, salt; bake in a lined 8×8 pan.

batch_totals.note: ≈9 brownies. Honey (~49 g sugar) is the main sugar; halving it drops each brownie by ~2.5 g sugar.

him.verdict: A genuinely goal-aligned dessert. At the tuned amounts each brownie is ~83 kcal with ~5.7 g protein — that's ~6.9 g protein per 100 kcal, elite for a sweet — from cottage + egg white (complete, high-absorption animal protein). Cocoa adds fiber, magnesium, iron and polyphenols. The main lever is honey (~5.4 g sugar/brownie); the peanut butter is the calorie-dense part (already moderated to 2 tbsp). Hits the sweet craving while actually contributing protein.
flags: ~6.9 g protein per 100 kcal (elite for a dessert)
honey is the main sugar (~5.4 g/brownie)
suggested_mods: For a leaner cut: drop honey to 2 tbsp (or swap half for stevia) — takes each brownie to ~75 kcal / ~4 g sugar
A scoop of chocolate protein powder in the batter lifts protein further and firms the texture
Cap the portion — small and moreish; log how many you eat

her_preconception.verdict: A nice better-for-her treat: complete protein + calcium (cottage), plus iron and magnesium from the cocoa, and honey's antioxidants. Baked (eggs cooked), pasteurized cottage — no safety flags. One minor note: cocoa contains a little caffeine/theobromine (~8 mg caffeine per brownie), so a few brownies still sit well under the pregnancy caffeine limit — just count it if she's also having coffee.
prenatal_highlights: complete protein + calcium from cottage cheese

safety_advisories.note: Cocoa has a little caffeine/theobromine (~8 mg caffeine/brownie) — count it toward the ~200 mg/day pregnancy caffeine limit if also drinking coffee.
safety_advisories.swap: fewer brownies / less cocoa if caffeine is close to the limit

suggested_mods: Great with berries (adds vitamin C) as a protein-forward dessert
Honey (not for infants, but fine for her) — moderate the amount for less sugar

cooking_guide: Blend the cottage cheese, egg whites, peanut butter and honey in a blender/food processor until completely smooth — blending out the cottage lumps is what gives the fudgy, not-grainy texture.
Add the cocoa powder, vanilla, baking powder and salt; blend again just until uniform and glossy.
Pour into a parchment-lined 8×8 pan and level the top.

Bake at 175 C (350 F) ~20-25 min — pull it when the top is set but the centre is still slightly soft (a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs). Overbaking makes protein brownies dry/rubbery, so err on the fudgy side.
Cool fully in the pan, then chill 1-2 hours before cutting — they firm up a lot cold and slice cleanly into 9.
Tip: a scoop of chocolate protein powder in the batter boosts protein and firms the texture; a spoon of cocoa nibs or a light swirl of extra peanut butter on top adds crunch/richness.
